top_choice_rationale: On public knowledge only, Cărtărescu (P001) offers the strongest combination under the common criteria: a distinctive voice, formal ambition at the scale of the whole book, imaginative depth, and a sustained project across decades. The Blinding trilogy and Solenoid appear to approach memory, the body and dream through different constructions, which suggests re-approach rather than mere enlargement. I cannot verify that, and I have read no texts for this ballot. The citation should rest on the major prose, with the poetry named only as a root, because my coverage of the poetry and early work is thin. The main unresolved reservations are that the linguistic achievement reaches me through translation of dense Romanian prose, and that the longest late books may show excess rather than architecture. Michon (P004) is second because his case is the most language-centered, though a slender, narrow corpus fits the whole-oeuvre standard less well. Can Xue (P002) is third for the completeness of her break with realist psychology, but I cannot show development across a partly translated corpus. Zurita (P003) is fourth because I cannot confirm that the printed poems carry the case without the extra-textual interventions, and poetry loses the most in translation. I rank all four above no award (P000) because each is a credible single-writer candidate. Support counts, fame, nationality and translation reach are not treated as merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. The profile records no tie to any shortlisted writer beyond ordinary committee colleagueship. My ekphrastic practice and Selma Lagerlöf work are context only, and I note that my practice is close to the art-history subject of Michon's work as a reason for caution, not as evidence for or against him. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
